apparatus.basis: Single-letter restoration within recoverable Greek loanword ζωγραφέω 'paint'; rest of word visible.
Continuation of verb ⲭⲓ 'take/receive' visible at start of next line as ⲧⲩ̄ (= -ⲧϥ); standard pair with preceding ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'release.'
Single-letter restoration in standard compound ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲛⲉ/ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'light' or 'manifestation'; here = ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'light' (the 'region of light').
Editor's restoration; the verbal idiom ⲥⲉⲍⲉ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ 'set on (their) feet' is attested in glossary.
Two letters restored within ⲧⲛⲁⲟ̄ 'the great' (Lyc. = ⲛⲟϭ), well-attested formula 'the great icon.'
Restoration within Greek loanword ⲕⲁⲧⲏⲭⲟⲩⲙⲉⲛⲟⲥ; remainder of word visible at start of next line.
Single-letter restoration; ⲡⲍⲙⲁⲧ = Lyc. ⲡϩⲙⲁⲧ 'the favor/grace/gift,' attested in glossary.
Editor's restoration; standard formulaic close 'unto eternity' (cf. ϣⲁ ⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ in glossary).
Editor's restoration; standard demonstrative formula 'that one' (= ⲉⲧⲙ̄ⲙⲉⲩ) following named figure.
Editor's restoration completing ⲁⲍⲱⲣⲣⲁⲫⲉ = ⲁⲍⲱⲣⲁⲫⲉ 'to paint' (Greek ζωγραφεῖν, with scribal doubling of ⲣ).
Single-letter restoration completing ⲟⲩⲱⲧ 'one, single' — opening word of phrase 'one in one place.'

Editor's restoration completing the verb ⲃⲱⲕ 'go.' The negation ⲉⲛ ('not') follows immediately. Approximately 10 chars lost before ⲃⲱⲕ; likely contained the future-form ⲡⲕⲁⲧⲏⲭⲟⲩⲙⲉⲛⲟⲥ ⲛⲁⲃⲱⲕ 'the catechumen shall (not) go.'
Editor's restoration; ~10 chars lost before ⲙⲡ-ⲉⲕⲗⲉⲕⲧⲟⲥ '[...] of the Elect.' Context demands a noun governing the genitive 'of the Elect' — perhaps 'the way' (ⲡⲙⲁⲓⲧ) or 'the salvation/raising.'

notes.decision: ⲟⲡ at the start of the page is the tail of a word continuing from the lost end of page 234. Possibly a remnant of ⲱⲡ 'count, reckon' or part of a compound; rendered as fragment '[...]op.'
Read as ⲁⲕ-ϣⲱⲡⲉ '(you) have come' (with Lyc. ⲁⲕ→ⲁ before ϣ), continuing the 2sg address to the Illuminator that runs through ⲁⲕⲟⲩⲱⲛⲍ̄, ⲁⲕⲍⲱⲣⲁⲫⲉ. The verb ϣⲱⲡⲉ ⲁ- 'come to' is standard.

Translated 'the Righteous one' on assumption that ⲡⲁⲓⲕⲁⲗⲟⲥ here = ⲡⲇⲓⲕⲁⲓⲟⲥ (Greek δίκαιος) with Lyc/scribal vowel shift ⲇⲓⲕⲁⲓ→ⲁⲓⲕⲁⲗ. Confirmed by context: this figure stands paired antithetically with ⲡⲣⲉϥⲣ̄ⲛⲁⲃⲉ 'the Sinner' in line 5 — the standard Manichaean righteous/sinner doublet for the soul-paths painted in the Picture-Book.
Read as ⲛ̄-ⲥⲉ-ⲧⲉϩⲟ 'and-they-cause-to-reach' (Lyc. ⲩ̄ for ⲥⲉ before ⲧ; cf. accumulated ⲧⲉϩⲟ 'reach, attain'). Causative-conjunctive: 'and they cause him to attain (the region of light).'
= ⲡⲣⲉϥ†ϩⲁⲡ 'the judge,' confirmed in glossary. Functions appositionally to the preceding ⲡⲕⲣⲓⲧⲏⲥ; the two terms (one Greek, one Coptic) name the same cosmic figure judging the dead.

Read as Lyc. ⲙⲟⲩϩⲉ 'burn, scorch' (Crum 207b) rather than ⲙⲟⲩϩ 'fill,' since the immediate cosmological context is Gehenna — the place of fire. The clause 'in which they habitually burn within forever' captures the eschatological torment proper to the Manichaean Gehenna.

3pl perfect 'they have painted' here functions impersonally/passively: 'these two have been painted' — referring back to the Righteous one and the Sinner the Illuminator depicted in the Great Icon. Could alternatively be a scribal slip for ⲁⲕⲍⲱⲣⲁⲫⲉ 'you have painted' (continuing the 2sg address); preserved as written.
Direct 2sg accusatorial question: 'But you — why have you not painted them?' The catechumen-disciple is challenging Mani directly about the asymmetry of the Picture-Book.

= ϩⲟ ϩⲓ ϩⲟ 'face by face / face-to-face' — the disciple's plea for direct visual recognition of the catechumen-soul's path within the icon, mirroring the categorical depictions of Righteous and Sinner.

The Illuminator's reply opens with a categorical denial: ⲙⲛ̄-ⲟⲁⲙ 'there is no power.' The reasoning given (lines 19-26) is that the catechumen's destiny varies place-by-place and depends on works performed with the Elect — too multiform to fix in a single image.
Read here as Greek ἐπειδή 'since, because,' introducing the causal clause justifying the impossibility. Distinct from the homograph ⲡⲉⲓⲁⲏ 'this end' (Lyc. ⲡⲉⲓ-ϩⲁⲏ).
= ϥⲥⲏϩ 'he is written/inscribed' (qualitative of ⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ 'write,' Lyc. ⲍ for ϩ, ⲩ for ϥ). The Elect's path is 'written in the icon' — affirming what was said in line 8 about the Righteous one.
